The imports for JUnit 5 and Mockito are missing. Probably the project uses JUnit 4 only. Simpler: remove JUnit5 annotations and Mockito extensions, and adjust imports. Also remove references to Mockito and use manual mock implementation (MockHoldingCostModel) already defined. The test uses @Mock and reset(mockHoldingCostModel) from Mockito. We can replace with manual mock.

Simplify: Remove imports for org.mockito and JUnit5. Use only JUnit4 imports: org.junit.*; org.junit.Assert.*; org.junit.Before; org.junit.After; org.junit.Test. Already imported org.junit.*; static org.junit.Assert.*; but also imported org.junit.* includes Before, After, Test, etc. However they also used @BeforeEach, @AfterEach, @DisplayName which are JUnit5. We'll replace those with JUnit4 equivalents: @Before for setupBeforeEach, @After for teardownAfterEach, and remove @DisplayName annotations (or replace with comments). Also remove @ExtendWith annotation.

Also need to fix references to HoldingCostModel interface. It seems Position has a field holdingCostModel of type CostModel? Actually earlier they imported org.ta4j.core.analysis.cost.CostModel and ZeroCostModel. The test expects HoldingCostModel type, but maybe there is an interface HoldingCostModel extends CostModel? In the library, there is likely a HoldingCostModel interface. However compilation cannot find it. Perhaps the correct type is CostModel (for holding cost). In Position constructor, third argument is holdingCostModel of type CostModel (maybe HoldingCostModel). Let's check: Position constructor signature likely (TradeType type, CostModel transactionCostModel, CostModel holdingCostModel). So we can treat HoldingCostModel as CostModel. So replace HoldingCostModel with CostModel throughout test.

Thus modify: AbstractHoldingCostModel implements CostModel, not HoldingCostModel. All references to HoldingCostModel become CostModel.

Also adjust mockHoldingCostModel type: currently declared as CostModel mockHoldingCostModel; annotated @Mock. We'll just declare MockHoldingCostModel mockHoldingCostModel; no annotation. Use manual reset.

Remove Mockito import and reset calls.

Also adjust methods that use mockHoldingCostModel.setReturn etc; that's fine if mockHoldingCostModel is MockHoldingCostModel.

But earlier they also used mockHoldingCostModel variable of type CostModel. Change its type to MockHoldingCostModel.

Also need to adjust Position creation: new Position(TradeType.BUY, transactionCostModel, mockHoldingCostModel); works as CostModel.

Also adjust imports: remove duplicate import of NaN, remove org.mockito.* imports.

Also remove @DisplayName annotations (or replace with @Test with comment). JUnit4 doesn't support DisplayName, we can just comment.

Also remove @BeforeEach, @AfterEach annotations and rename methods to @Before and @After.

But there are also @Before and @After methods at bottom (setUp and tearDown). Duplicate. We'll consolidate: Keep only one setUp and tearDown using @Before and @After. Remove the earlier @BeforeEach/@AfterEach methods.

Simplify: Remove the methods setupBeforeEach and teardownAfterEach, and rely on setUp and tearDown.

But tests rely on mockHoldingCostModel being reset before each test; setUp does that. So we can delete the earlier ones.

Also need to adjust import for Trade.TradeType: they used Trade.TradeType.BUY; but they also imported org.ta4j.core.Trade.TradeType earlier. They used both. In code they refer to Trade.TradeType.BUY. That's fine.

Now adjust code accordingly.

Let's produce corrected test class.
